direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires a from-scratch installable Six compatibility project with six.py, setup metadata, docs, and broad Python 2/3 compatibility APIs.
Parallel metadata reports actual parallel use, four subagents, successful process/protocol/artifact status, and 200 of 200 official quality.
Current completed status evaluation reports solution_passed true with counts passed 200, failed 0, total 200, and reward 1.0.
Official evaluation summary is completed and ok, with solution_passed true and 200 of 200 tests passed.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event journal records the parallel session lifecycle, tool transport, AgentSwarm launch, subagent completion, parent verification, and completed prompt.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the /workspace working directory and raw session directory.
Core subagent owned six.py, wrote an initial implementation, compared against six 1.16.0, replaced six.py with the reference source plus requested conditional, and verified behavior.
Packaging subagent created setup.py, setup.cfg, MANIFEST.in, tox.ini, .gitignore, changelog, contributors, license, and README metadata files, then verified setup.py name and version.
Documentation subagent created documentation/conf.py, index.rst, Makefile, and _static, compiled conf.py, built Sphinx HTML successfully, and cleaned build artifacts.
Test subagent created test_six.py, ran pytest while six.py was still changing, diagnosed early failures, fixed test assumptions, and reached stable 75-passed verification.

Parallel parent inspected the workspace, launched four subagents, consumed their aggregate result, listed the final files, ran pytest, smoke tests, setup parsing, and pip install verification before final response.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event journal records the serial single-agent session lifecycle, tool transport, verification steps, cleanup, and completed prompt.
Session index maps the serial session id to the /workspace working directory and raw session directory.

Serial actor wrote six.py in chunks, fixed core bugs, created packaging and docs, verified setup, install, all 15 nodes, cleaned editable-install contamination, and returned a completed final response.

parallel.requirements: The run recognized the full Six project: versioned six.py API, moves mappings, byte/text helpers, method helpers, syntax shims, metaclass helpers, unittest shims, packaging, docs, and verification.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent chose four concurrent owners: core six.py, packaging/metadata, documentation, and tests, then retained final integration and verification responsibility itself.
parallel.implementation: The core child ultimately copied the real six 1.16.0 source and applied the requested Python 3.14 URLopener conditional; other children created packaging files, Sphinx docs, and a 75-test pytest suite.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Children wrote directly into the shared /workspace final tree. The parent accepted their returned summaries, listed final files, and delivered a tree containing six.py, metadata, docs, and test_six.py.
parallel.verification: Child-level checks included setup parsing, Sphinx build, and pytest. The parent reran pytest, smoke-tested imports and conversions, tested setup.py, performed a no-deps pip install/import/uninstall, and official evaluation passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No required task remained unfinished at closure. The only material coordination issue was transient: a verifier consumed an in-flight six.py that the core child later replaced.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same broad Six API and project-file obligations from the prompt, including setup metadata, docs, compatibility helpers, and final verification.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned all implementation, packaging, documentation, verification, cleanup, and final reporting, using a todo list for sequential progress.
serial.implementation: It wrote six.py in chunks, debugged smoke-test failures, then wrote setup.py, setup.cfg, MANIFEST.in, README, LICENSE, CHANGES, CONTRIBUTORS, tox.ini, and documentation files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because one actor owned the whole tree, integration was sequential. It cleaned build and editable-install byproducts and delivered a final tree without a persistent pytest suite.
serial.verification: It ran core smoke tests, setup.py name/version, editable install and import checks, a comprehensive inline all-15-node test script, and cleanup checks before final response; official evaluation passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official failure remained. The final narrative and workspace reported a 1.17.0 variant rather than exact 1.16.0, but the completed official evaluation still marked the solution as passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the requested Six compatibility APIs, package files, docs, and verification needs, and delegated them as separate scopes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same broad requirements and implemented a complete project sequentially.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both covered the evaluator-relevant obligations; parallel more explicitly targeted 1.16.0 plus the prompt's conditional, while serial reported a 1.17.0 variant but still passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent assigned four distinct child scopes: six.py, packaging, documentation, and tests, while the parent owned final integration and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: One actor kept all scopes in a local todo list and completed them sequentially.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained parallel throughput but exposed cross-agent coordination on the shared deliverable; serial avoided child handoffs and write concurrency.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs were detailed and mostly non-overlapping, but the verifier brief explicitly assumed another child would provide six.py while work happened concurrently.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor carried one evolving implementation context and did not transfer interface assumptions across children.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel transferred enough requirements for success, yet the test child's interface to six.py was a live shared file rather than a stable handoff; serial used one local state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Core implementation evolved from a memory-written file to a copied six 1.16.0 reference with a prompt-required URLopener conditional.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented its own single-file compatibility library, fixed observed bugs, and then added support files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel converged by replacing six.py with the upstream source plus a small conditional, while serial used an independently written implementation that reported version 1.17.0 but passed official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child results returned to the parent through AgentSwarm, and the parent inspected the aggregate before final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child lifecycle existed; the single actor advanced from local implementation to local verification and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a real join point and consumed returned work; serial had no delegated result retrieval risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children wrote directly to the same /workspace final tree; the core child replaced six.py while the test child was already using that file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also used /workspace but with one writer, then cleaned its own editable-install artifacts before finishing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material shared-state difference is the parallel deliverable overwrite during verification; serial's shared state was sequential and self-contained.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed child tests, then parent-level pytest, smoke imports, setup parsing, and pip install/import validation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed smoke tests, setup parsing, editable install/import checks, and an inline all-15-node verification script.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had enough acceptance evidence for official pass; parallel had a broader persistent pytest suite while serial used inline comprehensive checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished in 1064.266 cell seconds after one AgentSwarm call, all children returned, and the parent closed with tests passing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in 1768.07 cell seconds without delegation and closed after completing its todo list and final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more agents and tokens but less elapsed cell time; neither run timed out or closed with unfinished required work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: the current completed cell/status.json evaluation marks both parallel and serial as solution_passed true. The concrete task-solving difference is strategic, not outcome-determining: parallel decomposed the work and later verified the joined tree, while serial implemented and verified sequentially.
parallel_contributors: Four scoped children created core, packaging, docs, and tests, and the parent reran integrated pytest plus smoke/install checks.
A transient overwrite of six.py during verification caused rework but was corrected before final acceptance.
serial_contributors: Single-actor ownership avoided child handoff and write-concurrency risks.
Serial ran an inline all-15-node verification script and cleanup before final closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered a six.py explicitly reporting 1.16.0; serial's final narrative reported a 1.17.0 variant even though the official evaluator still passed it.
Parallel retained a persistent test_six.py suite in the artifact; serial verified with inline tests and did not retain test_six.py.
evaluator_effects: Serial status counts include a failed field alongside passed 200, total 200, reward 1.0, and solution_passed true; the current solution_passed field controls the pair relation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an observed parallel adverse process episode, not an explanation for a failed solution

The parent explicitly owned final integration/verification after child returns and inspected the combined tree.
Final deliverable placement was owned by children writing assigned files and by the parent checking the assembled workspace.
The parent controlled the end-to-end pipeline from delegation through final pytest, smoke tests, install check, and final response.
Implementation was not blocked behind one serial preflight; core, packaging, documentation, and tests were launched together.
The parallel run did not complete an investigation phase before implementation; children directly wrote implementation, docs, metadata, and tests.
The indispensable core path had an active owner and finished; no evidence shows capacity diverted from required implementation work.
Four children did not exhaust the finite budget; all returned and the parent still had time for integrated verification.
The largest core child completed and verified its assigned six.py work; there was no unfinished overbroad child task at closure.
Child briefs included the relevant task, acceptance, and file-scope facts; the verifier's problem came from a changing file, not a missing known requirement.
The scopes specified file ownership and expected APIs; there was no unresolved incompatible interface contract between separately produced components.
No known finding disappeared through a summary or transfer; the parent received child summaries and used them for verification.
The AgentSwarm return was long but the parent reduced it and ran concrete acceptance checks, so no needed information remained unconsumed.
No parent action is shown consuming a superseded child handoff; the observed stale-state symptom was the verifier using a live file before replacement.
Children did not return incompatible reports that remained unadjudicated; all final summaries were compatible and parent checks passed.
The parent did not accept completion solely from child returns; it ran integrated pytest, smoke imports, setup parsing, and pip install checks before final response.
There was no replacement child or repeated retry lacking inherited checkpoint state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child was explicitly stopped or cancelled before needed work finalized; all four child results returned completed.
A complete candidate was not left unpromoted at closure; the final workspace was assembled, verified, and officially passed.
The parent's final pytest, smoke, and install checks occurred after child results returned and after the final tree was listed.
Completed implementation work from children was present in the final tree and was used in parent-level verification.
The verifier child returned concrete pytest results and the parent then reran the tests itself.
Transient child test failures were handled by the verifier and final parent checks; no required failed child scope was abandoned.
The parent received and acted on the completed child results, including rerunning tests and smoke checks.
The parent did not wait until timeout without inspection; it resumed after child completion and ran active verification well before closure.
Children wrote different assigned files, but there were no competing cross-file designs claiming the same behavior that required unresolved reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source file and reconciled a same-file edit; the verifier read six.py while the core owner replaced it.
The overwritten path was the required entry-point deliverable six.py, so the more specific Deliverable Overwrite label applies.
Agent-0 replaced /workspace/six.py with a copied reference source while agent-3 was already running and debugging pytest against that required entry-point file.
candidates.realized_consequence: The verifier's first pytest collection failed on the in-flight deliverable and the verifier spent extra cycles treating it as a possible library bug before rerunning after the replacement.
candidates.near_match_reason: The verifier consumed a live artifact, but the directly evidenced causal boundary is the concrete replacement of the required entry-point file during verification.

candidates.reason: There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple final outputs from another agent.
The workspace was shared, but the concrete adverse event is better classified as a deliverable overwrite rather than generic unisolated writes.
The verifier did consume a changing generated file, but the same chain has a more specific directly evidenced Deliverable Overwrite on the required six.py entry point.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent launched a core writer and verifier concurrently; the verifier found and tested six.py, then the core writer replaced that required entry-point deliverable, invalidating the verifier's first failure diagnosis and forcing reruns.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The verifier's first pytest collection failed on the in-flight deliverable and the verifier spent extra cycles treating it as a possible library bug before rerunning after the replacement.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Artifact leakage is a symptom, but Deliverable Overwrite is more specific because the required entry-point file was concretely replaced while another child was verifying it.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Artifact Leakage was suppressed for the same shared six.py episode because Deliverable Overwrite is the more specific concrete write boundary.
Unisolated Workspace Writes and Source Overwrite were suppressed for the same chain because the affected path was the required entry-point deliverable.
